one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event in the window: Q3 FY2027 results (quarter ended 2026-10-31), expected around Nov 18-25 (last year's Q3 print was 2025-11-19 [6]; date not yet confirmed). Guide revenue 1.90-1.98B and adjusted EPS 4.33-4.79 [3]; Street 4.33 (Zacks) to 4.67 (Earnings Whispers [10]); whisper 4.55, 80% range 4.24-4.86 [27]. A beat is likely (three straight EPS beats vs guide [3,4,5]) but the stock fell 11.5% on the Q2 beat-and-raise because of the FY27 Communications cut, so the reaction hinges on FY28 commentary (wireless recapture, BEAD start, carrier programs) more than the quarter. Short-horizon base rates pull both ways: deeply negative 6-month momentum (-56% from June; new lows Oct 20-21 [14]) vs short-term reversal and September insider buying at ~$281-297 [14]. I stay near neutral: lognormal centred at $223 (+0.9%) with a 17% monthly sigma (usual 0.53/3.5 = 15%, lifted for the print).

fair_value.method: Research target (12m) 289.81: approved backlog-and-capacity driver build (horizon NTM EPS ~$23, adj EBITDA ~1,370) valued at an exit P/E of 12.1x (w 0.6) and EV/EBITDA 8.6x (w 0.4), both shrunk from today's discount toward the peer median with k = 0.8; net debt includes 367 of supplier finance.

downside.story: 10th percentile: carriers cut fiber programs (MTZ-style Communications cut; AT&T+Verizon 30.5% of revenue), NTM backlog 12% below path, Communications margin -200bp, data-center work pauses (standing AI-capex low case: 2028 capex -9%), Building Systems share -30% and margin -300bp; multiple compresses 2 turns toward DY's 2019 trough (P/E 10.1x, EV/EBITDA 6.6x).

base.story: Median: the approved drivers (FY27 revenue 7,656 / EPS ~18.3, FY28 8,366 / ~20.1, FY29 9,237 / ~23.2), carrier programs and BEAD hold the Communications backlog on its path, data-center market at or below the standing AI-capex base; the multiple recovers only the 20% of its peer gap the k rule allows (P/E 11.1x -> 12.1x).

upside.story: 90th percentile: BEAD construction and long-haul/AI fiber ramp lift NTM backlog 8% above path, wireless deferral recaptured, Communications margin +100bp, Building Systems share +15% as labor adds; AI-capex fear fades and the multiple re-rates 4 turns toward the peer median (P/E 16.1x, EV/EBITDA 12.6x).

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E whole-company 16.4-35.2x (MTZ, PRIM, PWR; median 17.1x); Building Systems segment peers 10.0-20.2x (median 15.75x); revenue-weighted 16.8x. Forward EV/EBITDA: no consensus; estimated 10.4x from trailing 10.0-14.5x (median 12.35x) / 1.187.
comps_summary.own_multiple: NTM P/E 11.1x (221.05 / (0.25 x 17.06 + 0.75 x 20.77 = 19.84), StockAnalysis); NTM EV/EBITDA 8.2x on the model
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Exit P/E 12.1x = 28% below the 16.8x weighted median; EV/EBITDA 8.6x = 17% below 10.4x. The k = 0.8 shrink keeps most of today's discount.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No extra discount beyond the k rule. Persisting reasons for the discount the rule keeps: 30.5% of revenue from two carriers (AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%), net debt ~2.5x adj EBITDA incl. supplier finance vs net-cash or low-levered peers, and amortization-excluded EPS (adjusted basis like MTZ/PWR, unlike EME).
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 7 peers, only 3 whole-company (MTZ, PWR, PRIM): no other listed US/European contractor is mainly carrier fiber/wireless construction (Circet, Ervin Cable, etc. are private); EME, MYRG, STRL, LMB match Building Systems only (~21% of revenue) and are kept segment-only; FIX and IESC lacked usable forward figures in the run table and were not added.

thesis_break_reason: $160 (-28%) is ~8x the Street NTM EPS of ~$19.8 and below the 2025 pre-AI range, a level that would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than volatility: a major carrier (AT&T 20.1% / Verizon 10.4% of revenue) cutting or re-sourcing a fiber program, backlog falling y/y, or a data-center pause hitting Building Systems, any of which would push leverage (net debt ~2.5x adj EBITDA incl. supplier finance) toward covenant-relevant levels. The 2018-19 analog (guide cut -> stock -62% over 13 months [11,13]) shows such breaks keep running.

key_uncertainties: Whether the 2026 de-rating (DY -56%, MTZ -53%, STRL -60% from June; PWR -14%, EME -18% [12]) is an AI-capex sentiment shock that mean-reverts or the start of an orders roll-over; base rates for industrial contractors say multiples stay compressed for most of a year after such moves (the k-rule keeps 80% of the gap).
Communications backlog path FY28-29 (comms_ntm_backlog +10%/+7%): MTZ's ~$400M Communications cut [16] and DY's wireless deferral are the 2026 base-rate evidence against it; -10% backlog = -8% value.
Carrier concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% of Q2 FY27 revenue [1]; AT&T's purchase of Lumen's consumer fiber concentrates it further.
Data-center construction (dc_mkt) after 2027: the standing AI-capex file's low case has 2028 spend -9% [24]; Building Systems is ~21% of revenue but ~30% of segment EBITDA.
Supplier finance growth (226 -> 367 in six months [8]) flattering operating cash flow.

sbc_treatment.note: Adjusted EPS excludes only amortization; SBC (0.53% of revenue) is deducted inside corporate_ebit, so sbc_pct_rev is 0 in the engine to avoid double counting; shares net -0.5%/yr after SBC issuance. Peers MTZ/PWR also report adjusted EPS ex amortization.

reasoning: Lane: base rates. (1) What happened: DY peaked at $566 after the May-2026 Q1 beat, then fell with the whole AI-infrastructure contractor group (MTZ -53%, STRL -60% from June; Corning -13% on 2026-09-14 [17]; OpenAI-spending scare in April [26]) and took a second leg down on its own Q2 print (-11.5%) when FY27 Communications was cut ~$160M; new lows on Oct 20-21 with no company news [14]. MTZ's July Communications cut (~$400M [15,16]) says carrier spend was lumpy industry-wide, not DY-specific. (2) History: the closest own analog is FY2019, when a guide cut (FY EPS -44% [13]) started a -62% drawdown that kept going for 13 months [11]; the 2017 and 2022 dips recovered within a year. So a de-rated DY does not mean-revert reliably; I keep the k = 0.8 rule's persistence (exit P/E 12.1x vs 11.1x today, peers 16.8x). (3) Fundamentals: I accept the approved quarterly driver set (FY27 EPS ~18.3, +7% vs StockAnalysis 17.06; FY28 ~20.1, -3% vs 20.77 and +6% vs Zacks 18.98; Q3 FY27 EPS 5.20 vs guide 4.33-4.79 and whisper 4.55); my only disagreement is that the Communications backlog path is at the optimistic end of the base rate (flag, -8% value if backlog runs 10% lower). The data-center market path sits at or below the standing AI-capex base. (4) Macro odds: Kalshi prices a 2027 US recession at 20% [18,19]; BEAD final proposals are all approved [20], so construction in 2027 is the main upside catalyst. (5) Result: research target (12m) of about $290, P10 about $135 and P90 about $499: a fatter left tail (log-vol 0.60 vs 0.43) for 2.5x leverage incl. supplier finance and 30% two-carrier concentration, with an average spread near the stock's 53% realized vol. Today's price remains the better 12-month point forecast; the target is one leg. Not driver-linked: none (both legs read the build). Research was web-limited (Nasdaq consensus API blocked; sec.gov read via XBRL and WebFetch).

model_inputs.ebit_basis_note: EBIT = GAAP operating income + amortization of intangibles (the company's Adjusted EPS excludes only amortization; SBC is a cost). Check Q2 FY27: revenue 2,005.9 - costs 1,813.9 = 192.0 + amortization 60.5 = 252.5 = segment adjusted EBITDA 315.5 - depreciation 55.2 - SBC 10.3 + 2.4 (gain on asset sales 2.3 and other items, which adjusted EBITDA takes out and other income carries). Segment 'ebit' rows hold segment ADJUSTED EBITDA; corporate_ebit = -(depreciation + SBC) + 2.5 a quarter; da = depreciation only (ex amortization), so engine EBITDA = adjusted EBITDA - SBC + ~2.5.

upside.story: 90th percentile: BEAD construction and long-haul/AI fiber ramp lift NTM backlog 8% above path, wireless deferral recaptured, Communications margin +100bp, Building Systems share +15% as labor adds; AI-capex fear fades and the multiple re-rates 4 turns toward the peer median (P/E 16.1x, EV/EBITDA 12.6x).

model_inputs.structure_note: Value is carried by two horizon-multiple legs on the approved backlog-and-capacity driver build (quarterly; Communications = backlog burn, Building Systems = data-center construction market x share): NTM P/E 12.1x (w 0.6) and NTM EV/EBITDA 8.6x (w 0.4), both exit multiples shrunk toward the peer median with k = 0.8. No DCF leg (policy). Drivers, quarters, driver_build and shareholder_returns are the approved set unchanged; my base-rate view moves only the multiples and the scenario deltas.
model_inputs.gap_note: (1) Method-fit flag 'filings too thin' is an XBRL tagging gap (no market-cap/operating-income tags), not a thin business: TTM revenue 6,880 (F6) and 10+ years of filings exist, so multiples are not weakened and no extra non-multiple leg is added. (2) Judgment calls for Kilian, against the approved drivers by id (not in the set): comms_ntm_backlog FY28 +10.4% is at the optimistic end of the base rate (MTZ cut FY Communications ~$400M in Jul-2026; DY deferred ~$150M wireless); backlog -10% in every forecast quarter = 266 vs 290 (-8%). bs_share -15% = 274 (-5.5%). comms_margin -100bp = 268 (-8%). (3) Supplier finance 367.4 added to net debt (-$12/share vs leaving it as working capital). (4) Possible financing: none above 20% probability found (net debt/adj EBITDA ~2.5x, FCF positive); a further bolt-on deal funded with debt is <20% and not modeled. (5) fair_value.value = engine base horizon value.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Exit P/E 12.1x = 28% below the 16.8x weighted median; EV/EBITDA 8.6x = 17% below 10.4x. The k = 0.8 shrink keeps most of today's discount.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No extra discount beyond the k rule. Persisting reasons for the discount the rule keeps: 30.5% of revenue from two carriers (AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%), net debt ~2.5x adj EBITDA incl. supplier finance vs net-cash or low-levered peers, and amortization-excluded EPS (adjusted basis like MTZ/PWR, unlike EME).
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 7 peers, only 3 whole-company (MTZ, PWR, PRIM): no other listed US/European contractor is mainly carrier fiber/wireless construction (Circet, Ervin Cable, etc. are private); EME, MYRG, STRL, LMB match Building Systems only (~21% of revenue) and are kept segment-only; FIX and IESC lacked usable forward figures in the run table and were not added.
